Generated from the clap definition of the `modelspec` command line in [`crates/modelspec-cli/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/modelspec/blob/main/crates/modelspec-cli/src/lib.rs) by `modelspec-docs`. It lists only commands that exist.

> Compile, check, train and run .mspec models

`modelspec --version` prints its version, and `--help` after any command prints the text below.

## Exit status

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | success |
| `1` | diagnostics or a runtime error |
| `2` | a usage error |

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`modelspec check`](#modelspec-check) | Parse and type-check a `.mspec` file |
| [`modelspec compile`](#modelspec-compile) | Compile a `.mspec` file into an artifact directory: artifact.json and, for Vulkan, its SPIR-V kernel modules |
| [`modelspec data`](#modelspec-data) | Prepare the training data of a masked-language-model run |
| [`modelspec data prepare`](#modelspec-data-prepare) | Copy a WikiText-103 raw release's wiki.train.raw and wiki.valid.raw into the Train and HeldOut splits and write their record, dataset.json |
| [`modelspec data tokenizer`](#modelspec-data-tokenizer) | Train the WordPiece tokenizer on the Train split of a prepared dataset to an exact vocabulary size and write its record |
| [`modelspec data pack`](#modelspec-data-pack) | Encode both splits of a prepared dataset with a tokenizer into sequences of an exact length and write them, their binding and their record with the held-out unigram baseline |
| [`modelspec infer`](#modelspec-infer) | Run the forward program of a `.mspec` model with the parameters of a checkpoint |
| [`modelspec inspect-device`](#modelspec-inspect-device) | Print the profile and negotiation verdict of each Vulkan physical device |
| [`modelspec ir`](#modelspec-ir) | Print the IR of a `.mspec` file at a stage |
| [`modelspec observe`](#modelspec-observe) | Replay a recorded run file over the event stream of `train --serve` |
| [`modelspec train`](#modelspec-train) | Train a `.mspec` model |

## `modelspec check`

Parse and type-check a `.mspec` file

```text
Usage: modelspec check <PATH>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | The .mspec file to check. |

## `modelspec compile`

Compile a `.mspec` file into an artifact directory: artifact.json and, for Vulkan, its SPIR-V kernel modules

```text
Usage: modelspec compile [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
       --output <DIR> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | yes | none | The .mspec file to compile. |
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend the artifact is for. One of:<br/>`cpu`: The CPU interpreter: an artifact without kernel modules<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute: an artifact with one SPIR-V module per kernel, in a build with the vulkan feature |
| `--output <DIR>` | yes | none | The artifact directory to write, created with its parents; files of an earlier artifact in it are overwritten. |
| `--device-profile <PATH>` | no | none | With --backend vulkan, schedule the plan within the limits of the DeviceProfile JSON file PATH (the form `inspect-device --format json` prints: its workgroup invocations and workgroup memory, recorded in the manifest as matmul_limits) and build the kernel modules for it, instead of scheduling for every device and probing device 0. |
| `--fast-math` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, compile with fast_math (DESIGN.md ADR-008): the manifest and every kernel cache key record it, and the float multiplies, adds and subtracts of the matmul, reduction, loss-sum and SGD kernels carry no NoContraction, so a driver may contract them into fused multiply-adds. |

## `modelspec data`

Prepare the training data of a masked-language-model run

```text
Usage: modelspec data <COMMAND>
```

## `modelspec data prepare`

Copy a WikiText-103 raw release's wiki.train.raw and wiki.valid.raw into the Train and HeldOut splits and write their record, dataset.json

```text
Usage: modelspec data prepare --out <DIR> <CORPUS>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<CORPUS>` | The directory holding the release's wiki.train.raw and wiki.valid.raw; nothing is downloaded. |
| `--out <DIR>` | The directory to write train.raw, heldout.raw and dataset.json into; created when missing. |

## `modelspec data tokenizer`

Train the WordPiece tokenizer on the Train split of a prepared dataset to an exact vocabulary size and write its record

```text
Usage: modelspec data tokenizer --dataset <DIR> --vocab-size <N>
       --out <FILE>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dataset <DIR>` | The dataset directory `data prepare` wrote; only its train.raw is read. |
| `--vocab-size <N>` | The number of tokens of the vocabulary, the five special tokens included. |
| `--out <FILE>` | The file to write the tokenizer record to, as JSON. |

## `modelspec data pack`

Encode both splits of a prepared dataset with a tokenizer into sequences of an exact length and write them, their binding and their record with the held-out unigram baseline. The record's packed_id is the version-8 UUID of the blake3 hash over the Train and the HeldOut content hashes and the sequence length as 8 little-endian bytes, in that order.

```text
Usage: modelspec data pack --dataset <DIR> --tokenizer <FILE>
       --seq-len <S> --out <DIR>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dataset <DIR>` | The dataset directory `data prepare` wrote. |
| `--tokenizer <FILE>` | The tokenizer record `data tokenizer` wrote. |
| `--seq-len <S>` | The number of tokens of every sequence; the partial tail of each split is dropped. |
| `--out <DIR>` | The directory to write train.tokens, heldout.tokens, binding.json and packed.json into; created when missing. |

## `modelspec infer`

Run the forward program of a `.mspec` model with the parameters of a checkpoint

```text
Usage: modelspec infer [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
       --checkpoint <PATH> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | yes | none | The .mspec file whose forward program runs. |
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend that runs the forward program. One of:<br/>`cpu`: The CPU interpreter<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute on one device, in a build with the vulkan feature |
| `--checkpoint <PATH>` | yes | none | The .msckpt file whose parameters the forward program reads. |
| `--device <INDEX>` | no | none | With --backend vulkan, run on the physical device INDEX, in the order the Vulkan loader lists them, instead of device 0. |

## `modelspec inspect-device`

Print the profile and negotiation verdict of each Vulkan physical device

```text
Usage: modelspec inspect-device [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend whose devices are inspected. One of:<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute |
| `--device <INDEX>` | no | none | The index of one physical device, in the order the Vulkan loader lists them; without it every device is printed. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | `text` | The output format. One of:<br/>`text`: One `<field>: <value>` line per field, then the negotiation verdict<br/>`json`: The profile's JSON form, or a JSON array of profiles |

## `modelspec ir`

Print the IR of a `.mspec` file at a stage

```text
Usage: modelspec ir --stage <STAGE> <PATH>
```

Every argument is required and has no default.

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | The .mspec file to lower. |
| `--stage <STAGE>` | The IR level to print. One of:<br/>`tensor`: Tensor IR after lowering and dead-code elimination<br/>`training`: Training IR: the Tensor IR with its reverse pass and SGD step attached<br/>`kernel`: Kernel IR: the kernels of the training step, its step plan and its forward plan, each dispatch with its FLOP and byte count |

## `modelspec observe`

Replay a recorded run file over the event stream of `train --serve`

```text
Usage: modelspec observe [OPTIONS] <PATH>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | yes | none | The recorded run file to replay, as `modelspec train --record` writes it. |
| `--serve <ADDR>` | no | `127.0.0.1:0` | Serve the replay as text/event-stream at path /events of ADDR, a loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8080 or localhost:8080 (port 0 picks a free one); the process serves until SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, then exits 0. |
| `--ui <DIR>` | no | none | Also serve the built observatory UI in DIR (ui/dist after `task ui`) at path / of ADDR; the directory is read whole before ADDR is bound. |

## `modelspec train`

Train a `.mspec` model

```text
Usage: modelspec train [OPTIONS] --backend <BACKEND> <PATH>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PATH>` | yes | none | The .mspec file to train. |
| `--backend <BACKEND>` | yes | none | The backend that runs the training step. One of:<br/>`cpu`: The CPU interpreter<br/>`vulkan`: Vulkan compute on one device, in a build with the vulkan feature |
| `--serve <ADDR>` | no | none | Stream the run's events as text/event-stream at path /events of ADDR, a loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8080 or localhost:8080 (port 0 picks a free one); the process keeps serving after the run until SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, then exits with the run's status. |
| `--record <PATH>` | no | none | Record the run's events to the file PATH, one JSON RunEvent per line in sequence order, the events --serve streams; `modelspec observe PATH` replays it. |
| `--ui <DIR>` | no | none | With --serve, also serve the built observatory UI in DIR (ui/dist after `task ui`) at path / of ADDR; the directory is read whole before ADDR is bound. |
| `--data <DIR>` | no | none | Train on the data of DIR instead of synthetic data. A DIR that holds binding.json is a packed directory of `modelspec data pack`: each input and target declaration names a tensor of the masked-language-model batch (ids, positions, key_mask, labels, weights), declared [B, S] or [B*S], and step K feeds the Train batch of step K. Any other DIR holds dense f32 files: NAME.f32 for the input and the target declaration NAME, row-major little-endian, and an optional order.u32 of sample indices. |
| `--init <DIR>` | no | none | Start each parameter that has a file DIR/P.f32, P its path without the model name, from that file instead of its initializer. |
| `--eval <DIR>` | no | none | After the last step, run the forward program over every sample of DIR, dense f32 files laid out as for a dense --data, and print `eval loss=<mean loss> accuracy=<fraction>`; beside a packed --data directory it is a usage error. |
| `--steps <N>` | no | none | Run N steps instead of the steps of the file's train block; a resumed run ends at its checkpoint's step plus N. |
| `--checkpoint <PATH>` | no | none | After the last step, write the parameters, step and optimizer to the .msckpt file PATH. |
| `--checkpoint-every <N>` | no | none | Also write STEM-K.msckpt beside the --checkpoint file at every step K after the start that is a multiple of N and before the end. |
| `--resume <PATH>` | no | none | Continue from the .msckpt file PATH: its parameters and step instead of the initializers and step 0, refused unless it matches the compiled file and its optimizer. |
| `--statistics-every <N>` | no | none | Take the norm and histogram of every parameter and its gradient for the event stream at the first step, every step that is a multiple of N and the last, instead of every 100; CPU only: a Vulkan run sends the Value entries of its first and last step and every other step's list empty. |
| `--device <INDEX>` | no | none | With --backend vulkan, train on the physical device INDEX, in the order the Vulkan loader lists them, instead of device 0. |
| `--stats` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, print the run's host waits, submits, dispatches, dispatches and barriers per step, bytes copied up and down, device allocations, peak device bytes, numerics class and microseconds per step on stderr after it. |
| `--profile` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, time every dispatch with GPU timestamp queries and print one `profile dispatch` line per dispatch site, with its FLOP, bytes, achieved GFLOP/s and GB/s, then per kernel of the plan the pipeline executable statistics the driver reports (`profile pipeline <kernel_module_id> executable <i> ...` lines, one per executable and one per statistic), or one `profile pipeline statistics: not reported` line on a device without VK_KHR_pipeline_executable_properties, with the reason in parentheses when the query fails, then the run's counters (dispatches, submits, host waits, barriers per step, bytes copied up and down, device allocations, peak device bytes), compile and pipeline creation time, steady-state microseconds per step and the step's total FLOP, bytes, GFLOP/s and GB/s on stderr after it. |
| `--fast-math` | no | `false` | With --backend vulkan, compile with fast_math (DESIGN.md ADR-008): the float multiplies, adds and subtracts of the matmul, reduction, loss-sum and SGD kernels may be contracted into fused multiply-adds, so the run is compared with the CPU within tolerance, never bit for bit; two runs of it on one device and driver give the same bits. |
